title: Ride dispatch with fakes and a metrics mock
name: Ride dispatch service

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how these tests use fakes and mocks to exercise the dispatch service, or in the service they test? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The metrics mock is created with relaxed = true. What does that mean for these tests?
choices: Calls to metrics methods that are never verified do not fail a test; only the explicit verify(...) assertions can fail
Any call to a metrics method not stubbed with every { ... } throws, so the tests prove no other metric is emitted
The mock records calls but verify(exactly = n) is ignored unless the answer is also stubbed
The service must call every method on the metrics interface at least once or the test fails

questions.prompt: In the first test, why does the test assert on gateway.offered instead of relying only on the returned DispatchResult?
choices: Because assertEquals on a data class compares only the first field, so extra offers would be missed
Because the fake gateway answers TimedOut for unscripted drivers, a service that sent extra offers could still return the same result, and only the recorded offers show it
Because the result is computed before any offer is sent, so it cannot reflect which drivers were contacted
Because Assigned("mid") is not comparable with the returned value unless the offers list matches

questions.prompt: The fakes and mocks are plain properties of DispatchServiceTest with no @BeforeEach and no @TestInstance annotation. Why doesn't state such as gateway.offered leak from one test to the next?
choices: MockK resets every fake registered in the class after each test
The fakes are immutable, so there is no state to leak
JUnit 5 creates a new instance of the test class for each test method by default, so the property initializers run again
The tests run in alphabetical order, and each one ends by clearing the lists
